title: The solo builder's production stack: n8n + Claude + Supabase + MCP
linkedinPost:
62% of startups have more than half their codebase written by AI. Half are building agents. (Supabase State of Startups, 2026.)

Most are choosing tools randomly — and rebuilding their stack every 3 months.

Here is what I would actually use:

n8n + Claude + Supabase + MCP. Not as a prototype layer. As the production system.

Why this combination specifically:

• n8n: EU data residency built in (Frankfurt, SOC2 certified). Code-native JavaScript nodes where no-code hits its ceiling. Native MCP server — Claude can orchestrate n8n workflows directly across 2,063 automation nodes.
• Supabase: Postgres with Row-Level Security at the schema layer. pgvector for RAG. Auth and edge functions included. One database that satisfies GDPR and EU AI Act Article 12 logging simultaneously.
• Claude API: route by cost (Haiku for simple tasks, Sonnet for complex reasoning) — keeps the inference bill under $100/month at production scale.
• MCP: 9,400+ servers in the official registry in 2026. The integration standard that makes the stack composable across any system your clients use.

In regulated financial services, this is also the DORA incident-logging architecture. Build one Supabase event log. Satisfy two regulatory obligations.

Revenue per employee rises when the operating model is designed around what AI does well — not when AI is added after the operating model is set.

Full piece + the Solo Stack four-layer decision table I use to evaluate alternatives — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: What is the n8n Claude Supabase stack and why do solo builders use it?

acceptedAnswer.text: The n8n Claude Supabase stack is a four-layer production architecture: n8n for workflow orchestration, Claude API for AI reasoning and generation, Supabase for data and auth, and MCP for live system integration. Solo builders use it because each layer is independently replaceable, total infrastructure cost is under $100/month at production scale, and EU data residency is built into both n8n and Supabase without configuration.

mainEntity.name: Is n8n better than Make or Zapier for AI workflows?

acceptedAnswer.text: For AI-native production builds, yes. n8n has EU data residency (Frankfurt, SOC2), native MCP server support connecting Claude directly to 2,063 automation nodes, and code-native JavaScript function nodes for typed pipeline contracts. Make and Zapier are adequate for simple automations but their AI integration depth, EU compliance posture, and code extensibility are weaker for production agentic systems.

mainEntity.name: How does Supabase Row-Level Security help with GDPR and EU AI Act compliance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supabase RLS enforces data access rules at the database layer — no application-level middleware required. For GDPR, it ensures each user accesses only their own data without custom enforcement logic. For EU AI Act Article 12, the same Postgres infrastructure can serve as the structured audit trail for AI decision logging, satisfying both regulatory requirements from one database without duplicating infrastructure.

mainEntity.name: Can this stack handle regulated financial services workloads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Papaya Global built a production HR compliance agent on Claude and Supabase with no engineers (SaaStr, 2026). For financial services specifically, the architecture supports credit memo automation, KYC document processing, and DORA-compliant incident logging — the three highest-ROI agentic use cases in regulated operations today. The EU data residency and RLS architecture are prerequisites most regulated clients will require anyway.
